mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts reflect strong consumer demand, boosting economic growth and S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts rise but SPX returns are negative in >40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE increases but SPX returns remain positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth doesn't translate to positive SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth exceeds inflation, real economic growth supports higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth outpaces CPIAUCSL but SPX returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 2%, tighter monetary policy may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 2% doesn't result in negative SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, low unemployment and accommodative policy boost S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4% and FEDFUNDS low but SPX returns negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment and falling unemployment indicate economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls but SPX returns are negative.
